summary.whatChanges: The Hono RPC client's `$ws()` method now builds WebSocket query strings through the same `buildSearchParams` option used by HTTP requests, instead of appending params manually. Custom serializers now apply to WebSocket URLs, and undefined query values are dropped. Tests cover both cases.
behaviorChanges: A custom `buildSearchParams` passed to `hc()` is now applied to `$ws()` URLs (e.g. arrays serialized as `tags[]=tag1&tags[]=tag2`) rather than being ignored
Query parameters with `undefined` values are omitted from the WebSocket URL instead of being stringified/appended
Default array handling for `$ws()` now follows the shared search-param builder rather than the inline append logic
Param replacement uses optional chaining, so a null-ish first argument no longer risks differing handling
risks: Existing apps relying on the old `$ws()` array encoding (repeated `key=value`) may now send a different query string if a custom builder is configured, breaking server-side parsing
Switching from `searchParams.set` to `append` could duplicate keys if the builder emits the same key more than once
Servers that previously received explicitly empty/undefined params will now see them absent
